prompt:
A full-fidelity desktop website homepage design comp, landscape, shown flat with no browser frame and no device. This is the website of Beauty From Ashes Surgical Ministry, a Christian nonprofit in the Carolinas that provides reconstructive plastic surgery, free or at reduced cost. Visual world (keep exactly): the page ground is a pale buff-grey salt-glazed stoneware surface with a fine orange-peel texture; headlines in a deep iron-brown dignified serif; small spaced-capital eyebrows; body text in a clean humanist sans; every clickable action is solid cobalt blue with a subtly hand-brushed edge; dividers are thin hand-brushed cobalt lines; amber and olive-green wood-ash glaze appears only in the photography. Layout, top to bottom:

1. NAVIGATION BAR (thin, full width): at left a text wordmark "Beauty From Ashes" in the serif with "SURGICAL MINISTRY" in small spaced capitals below; centered links "Our Mission", "How We Help", "Stories", "Get Involved", "Contact"; at right a small "EN | ES" switch and a solid cobalt button "Give". A hand-brushed cobalt line runs under the bar.

2. PHOTOGRAPHIC BAND (full width, about 35% of the height): a tight, edge-to-edge macro photograph of the shoulder and rim of a Carolina stoneware jar, glossy amber and olive-green wood-ash glaze running downward in long drips over speckled buff clay, soft natural side light. The drips point down toward the text below.

3. HELP SECTION (about 40% of the height) on the stoneware ground, two columns:
- LEFT 55%: eyebrow "A CHRISTIAN SURGICAL MINISTRY · CHARLOTTE & FORT MILL"; a large iron-brown serif headline on two lines "Restoring more than what can be seen."; a paragraph "Reconstructive plastic surgery, free or at reduced cost, for children and adults whose need exceeds their means. Open to everyone."; a solid cobalt button "Ask for help" and an iron-brown outlined button "Refer someone".
- RIGHT 45%: a quiet panel titled in serif "What happens when you ask" listing five steps, each number hand-brushed in cobalt: "1 Submit a request", "2 Initial review", "3 Conversation", "4 Decision", "5 Care and support". Thin brushed cobalt rules between steps.

4. MISSION (bottom 20%, partly visible): small spaced capitals "OUR MISSION" centered, then the beginning of a large centered italic serif quotation in iron brown: "To glorify God by serving every patient with Christlike compassion and surgical excellence, fostering healing that reaches beyond the physical…"

Overall: calm, dignified, professional, warm and hopeful; unmistakably a real nonprofit website with crisp, legible web typography. Not a church bulletin, not a cosmetic surgery advertisement, not a rustic boutique.
